newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian euthanasia law killed off.
newsitem.headline: Australian euthanasia law killed off.

text.p: Australia's world-first euthanasia law was quietly consigned to history on Thursday when the country's governor-general signed into law a bill outlawing assisted suicide in the Northern Territory.
Governor-General Sir William Deane had already rejected pleas from two terminally ill people to delay signing the bill for one or two weeks so they could use it to die.
"The governor-general gave assent to the bill this morning," Deane's official secretary told Reuters.
The federal bill, passed by parliament after heated debate early on Tuesday, strikes down the voluntary euthanasia law that came into operatin in the remote Territory last July.
Deane, who represents Britain's Queen Elizabeth as head of state, had said he could not justify departing from the usual routine of signing a bill as soon as all the paperwork was in.
Before the Senate passed the bill, pro-euthanasia senators tried to insert an exception to let two people, who had completed all legal formalities, kill themselves.
The bid failed, however, and the bill passed unamended to strike down the Northern Territory law as soon as Deane went through the formality of giving it "the Royal Assent".
Four people have committed assisted suicide since the law came into effect in July, using a computer-controlled machine that injected a lethal drug.
Euthanasia has remained illegal in the rest of Australia but supporters and opponents agree that it is widely practised.
The Northern Territory law was opposed by a wide coalition of church and civic leaers, even though polls show around 75 percent of Australians back the idea of euthanasia.
